title: Greece 1970: regime paths and civilian transition history review
scope: Historical design guidance only. No generator or runtime edits. All effect magnitudes and durations remain balance proposals requiring the existing MD code audit.

latest_draft_audit.verdict: Closed: the identified historical sequencing, amnesty-scope, civilian-government and active-repression issues are resolved. Remaining numerical effects and continuing justice-capacity costs are accepted design assumptions, not empirical historical claims.
passed: Three exclusive initial commitments; negotiated exits do not require a forced calendar collapse.
Permanent junta is possible; hardline reversal needs a real domestic contest, not a date.
Controlled opening keeps reserve powers, restricted public life and censure; no free democratic legitimacy.
A single 365-day review does not itself transfer power when it expires.
Regime packages replace incompatible rewards; no free bonus stacking across governments.
No compulsory foreign war or prescribed civilian election winner.

findings.finding: The trial milestone precedes the first free election. Historically the free election was 17 November 1974, while the archived Polytechnic trial opened on 16 October 1975.
findings.fix: Use Launch Independent Investigations plus actual court safeguards before elections. Substantive trials and verdicts can continue afterward; no completed conviction or prior broad amnesty is needed to permit voting.
findings.resolution: The early node now launches independent investigations. Its note explicitly permits trials and verdicts after the election; retirement guarantees likewise do not require every case or retirement to finish first.

findings.finding: Civilian party government is gated on the final constitutional package. This conflates civilian executive transfer, an electoral mandate and a completed constitution. The civilian cabinet existed from July 1974 and a parliamentary mandate from November, before the 1975 constitution.
findings.fix: Separate actual civilian executive, actual party mandate and completed constitution flags. Permit appropriate interim administration and then party programmes after an actual mandate. Retain full regime rewards until the implemented constitutional milestone.
findings.resolution: Civilian transfer is now a separate implemented flag. Civilian party gates accept transfer or the full constitutional regime while retaining actual party mandate requirements. The final regime bonuses still require a ratified civilian constitution.

findings.finding: The limited-amnesty scope remains undefined. Saying not universal does not explicitly preserve serious-abuse investigations and survivor remedies.
findings.fix: Define lesser or nonviolent political participation covered by the bargain. Preserve evidence, independent investigation and individual responsibility for torture and serious abuses, plus civil and compensation claims. A blanket-immunity bargain cannot count as full accountability.
findings.resolution: The limited settlement explicitly covers defined nonviolent or lesser participation. Torture and serious abuses remain individually investigable; evidence, civil claims and compensation survive both paths.

findings.finding: The general review is timed, but judicial casework has a lasting modifier with no completion/reassessment condition.
findings.fix: Call it funded continuing justice capacity if permanent; otherwise replace a transitional backlog modifier after real casework completion. Survivor compensation is not erased when trials finish.
findings.resolution: The modifier is explicitly continuing funded casework and victim obligations, rather than a permanent generic democracy penalty. It remains a proposed ongoing justice-capacity cost; no claim is made that a transitional backlog must last forever.

findings.finding: Maximum planning from decree authority and lower research from military rule are balance abstractions, not measured historical percentages.
findings.fix: Tie planning to actual funded command preparation and research limitations to implemented academic/exchange restrictions. Label all numerical effects proposed game balance; avoid claiming military government inherently plans better.
findings.resolution: Planning and research values remain explicit proposed game-balance abstractions in a design-only document. Command preparation is part of the stated rationale. These figures are not historical measurements or evidence of inherent regime superiority.

findings.finding: Inherited security institutions and unresolved harms differ from active arbitrary detention. A genuine rights milestone should not imply unchanged active torture remains necessary until final ratification.
findings.fix: If coercive practices have actually ended, replace that component with a named inherited-apparatus/claims burden until real reform. Keep remedies and evidence.
findings.resolution: Actual civilian transfer removes the active decree/security/reserve-power/restricted-life ideas and adds unresolved victim claims. Controlled opening also preserves claims, while retaining its restricted public-life and reserve-power burdens.

latest_draft_audit.limits: Chronology is sourced. Numerical costs, duration and alternative settlements are design proposals, not measured historical effects. No generator or runtime edits were made by this reviewer.

central_recommendation: Use three mutually exclusive institutional commitments for the current political phase: retained military rule, a controlled opening under reserve military/presidential powers, or a transfer to genuine civilian constitutional government. Named leaders and parties are a separate axis.

historical_constraints.fact: In January 1970 Papadopoulos is prime minister, Zoitakis is regent and Constantine II remains in exile. An opening in 1970 is an alternate policy, not the completed historical 1973 arrangement.
The 1973 Papadopoulos project combined a republic and extensive presidential authority. A civilian prime minister alone did not establish unrestricted parliamentary government.
Markezinis was prime minister while Papadopoulos was president in November 1973. Do not use one leader slot as proof that the armed forces lost their political veto.
On 25 November 1973 Ioannidis overthrew Papadopoulos. Ioannidis was the dominant figure behind formal President Gizikis and Prime Minister Androutsopoulos; these are distinct roles.

The actual civilian transition began in July 1974. The national-unity government preceded the November election and December constitutional referendum; an elected winner was not required before an interim civilian cabinet could exist.
The free referendum of 8 December 1974 rejected monarchy. A successful royal restoration is alternate history; it cannot be pre-awarded by an officer appointment or a managed plebiscite.
Post-dictatorship courts tried junta figures, including in the Polytechnic case. Accountability therefore has a concrete historical basis; it need not be invented as an obligatory civil war.

The 1973 intelligence assessment is a contemporary US estimate, including failed predictions and value judgements. Its account of internal factional power is useful; its forecasts are not deterministic event instructions.

paths.entry_condition: An actual junta controls the executive and coercive institutions. The player commits to preserving military political authority; no civilian election mandate is pretended.

leadership_subfork.title: Consolidate Papadopoulos's Coalition
leadership_subfork.gate: Papadopoulos actually leads the regime; officer support and appointments are resolved domestically.
leadership_subfork.benefit_intent: Preserve existing cabinet continuity and reduce the immediate cost of renegotiating command appointments.
leadership_subfork.cost_intent: Retain political exclusion, security expenditure, weak independent scrutiny and unresolved repression claims. No inherent military-quality bonus.

leadership_subfork.title: Back an Internal Hardline Challenge
leadership_subfork.gate: Ioannidis or another historically identified faction has actual organisation and support; resolve the domestic challenge before changing leadership.
leadership_subfork.benefit_intent: If successful, replace a contested incumbent and consolidate the challenger's existing network.
leadership_subfork.cost_intent: A real challenge consumes political resources and may disrupt command cohesion; success is not guaranteed, and harder repression does not solve inflation or administrative weakness.

long_term_choices: Military-directed development versus a technically autonomous civilian economic cabinet that still lacks sovereign political control.
Patronage appointments versus funded professional procurement; military rule need not force the same economic policy everywhere.
paths.historical_status: Continuation beyond 1974 is a deliberate alternate outcome. Neither the calendar nor a failed focus automatically removes it.
paths.recovery_rule: A later civilian opening requires a new transition procedure and replacement of incompatible regime packages, not collection of all three permanent reward sets.

paths.entry_condition: The incumbent military coalition accepts limited political opening while retaining specified reserve powers. In the historical 1973 version Papadopoulos becomes president and appoints Markezinis prime minister.

meaningful_subfork.title: Keep a Restricted Political Arena
meaningful_subfork.gate: The regime retains controls on eligibility and independent organisation.
meaningful_subfork.benefit_intent: Lower immediate concession and command-reorganisation costs; incumbent institutions retain predictable authority.
meaningful_subfork.cost_intent: Incomplete legitimacy and excluded opposition persist. A managed vote cannot clear the full repression or decree-rule penalties.

meaningful_subfork.title: Negotiate Wider Political Participation
meaningful_subfork.gate: Political rights are actually widened and invited civilian actors can independently accept, refuse or demand guarantees.
meaningful_subfork.benefit_intent: Build a wider negotiating coalition and prepare a possible lawful handover.
meaningful_subfork.cost_intent: Spend political capital, institutional reform time and money; hardline opponents may challenge the arrangement only if organised, not because of a scripted month.

outcomes: A sustained hybrid regime, explicitly marked as an authoritarian alternative.
A negotiated transfer after ending effective military vetoes and implementing civilian guarantees.
A conditional domestic hardline reversal if a real challenge succeeds; no automatic Ioannidis coup.
paths.reward_boundaries: A civilian cabinet can improve particular administration, but its appointment alone does not award free elections, full European rehabilitation or abolition of military interference.

paths.proposed_entry_title: Transfer Power to a Civilian Government
paths.entry_condition: A negotiated handover or actual domestic regime crisis creates an interim civilian authority and effective military obedience. This can precede a general election. Do not require a Cyprus war, defeat, predetermined collapse or a particular year.

required_milestones.title: Establish an Interim Civilian Cabinet
required_milestones.test: Actual domestic agreement or resolved authority transfer; record composition and remit. This cabinet is not automatically the elected long-term government.

required_milestones.title: Restore Freedom to Organise
required_milestones.test: Political organisation, press and assembly protections are implemented. Ending a party ban alone does not end emergency executive powers.

required_milestones.title: Bind the Armed Forces to Civilian Orders
required_milestones.test: Appointments, domestic security authority and chain of command are placed under accountable civilian institutions; review individual wrongdoing separately from service-wide collective punishment.

required_milestones.title: Hold an Implemented Competitive Election
required_milestones.test: Rules and civil liberties operate; derive government from actual support and agreed outcomes rather than a fixed Karamanlis or Papandreou victory.

required_milestones.title: Resolve the Constitutional Settlement
required_milestones.test: An actual free referendum or valid constitutional procedure determines Crown/republic and executive powers; respect a republican result.

temporary_costs: Fund court capacity, detainee review, record preservation and administrative audits; costs cease or change when the work is completed.
Spend political capital on a specified officer-retirement or appointment settlement; do not apply a universal combat penalty to every professional soldier.
Use temporary caretaker restrictions only while that cabinet actually has a limited mandate. An elected civilian government must not retain an endless generic caretaker penalty.
durable_benefits: Remove decree-rule and repression burdens as the corresponding institutions genuinely change.
Reward lawful succession, professional command, transparent procurement and broader political participation with bounded existing MD effects.
Enable renewed European institutional negotiations; admission, loans and foreign agreements remain conditional on real external acceptance.

accountability_fork.shared_entry: A civilian authority controls the courts and security chain of command; records are preserved and survivors can make claims.

exclusive_choices.title: Prosecute Individual Responsibility
exclusive_choices.requirements: Fund independent investigation and due process; distinguish leadership responsibility, torture, specific offences and ordinary service.
exclusive_choices.immediate_cost: Higher judicial staffing, archive and witness-protection expenditure; possible organised obstruction must be tied to real actors.
exclusive_choices.lasting_gain: Stronger institutional accountability and a clearer break with coercive political power after actual cases are resolved.
exclusive_choices.civil_claims: Preserve survivors' civil claims and access to evidence. No automatic execution, conviction of every officer, or collective purge.
exclusive_choices.historical_status: Trials have a historical basis; their speed, scope and outcomes are not fixed by a focus.

exclusive_choices.title: Negotiate Limited Amnesty and Retirement
exclusive_choices.requirements: A defined negotiated settlement for nonviolent political participation or specified lesser conduct; individual screening remains for serious abuses.
exclusive_choices.immediate_gain: Lower immediate command-reorganisation friction and a potentially faster agreed retirement timetable.
exclusive_choices.continuing_cost: Retained networks and a narrower reckoning require monitoring; do not award the full accountability package.
exclusive_choices.civil_claims: Keep civil compensation, evidence preservation and investigation of torture and grave abuses outside the amnesty. Victim claims are not deleted by a reconciliation flag.
exclusive_choices.historical_status: A design alternative, not a claim that the historical trials were unnecessary or that broad impunity was lawful.

accountability_fork.optional_harsh_alternative: If a blanket-immunity bargain is retained elsewhere, label it explicitly as contested impunity with continuing survivor claims, rights problems and institutional consequences. It cannot count as completed accountability or erase facts.

party_and_leader_gating: Keep regime commitment distinct from party programme. A controlled-opening cabinet cannot automatically access every civilian party's governing tree.
Karamanlis and Kanellopoulos are civilian conservative actors, not interchangeable formal heads of state. ERE and ND are contemporary formations, not a date-triggered automatic party conversion.
Mavros requires actual Centre leadership and governing authority; a broad liberal outlook alone is insufficient.

Andreas requires actual political leadership and lawful governing authority. PAK opposition in 1970 is not a government; PASOK requires actual party formation. Do not treat either as a compliant junta cabinet by default.

KKE legal participation does not imply KKE government. Its parliamentary route requires actual mandate/coalition authority; a revolutionary single-party takeover is a separate, explicitly resolved alternative.
Koligiannis and Florakis are actual leadership choices. Historical succession is a default chronology, not a mandatory automatic replacement.

A free constitutional monarchy is compatible with a civilian political government; Constantine II is not himself every monarchist party. Royal restoration is not a fourth way to silently retain military vetoes.

Public policy branches for shipping, rural development, public services and investment should remain available under the appropriate actual government without implying that only military rule can administer them.
state_transition_rules: Record a chosen institutional commitment separately from the achieved regime. A focus offering transfer is a proposal; actual handover is an outcome.
Only one current regime package may be active. When controlled opening becomes genuinely civilian, replace the hybrid package and its benefits/costs rather than stacking them.
Keep the visible major paths exclusive within a phase, with a named later reconsideration/transition milestone if policy genuinely changes. Prevent free toggling and repeated one-time grants.
Historically named 1973 arrangements need actual matching roles. Earlier counterparts can exist as clearly marked alternate developments.
No automatic collapse in July 1974, automatic student uprising, inevitable hardline coup or compulsory war with Turkey/Cyprus.
Domestic protest is a result of real grievances and freedoms/repression; peaceful participation does not require perpetual violent instability.
Ending a ban, appointing a civilian minister or announcing an election does not alone remove emergency powers. Removal gates must test the institution represented by each starting spirit.
No foreign human chooses Greece's domestic government. Foreign actors control their own recognition, aid, treaty acceptance and military actions.

draft_checks.check: The previous opening allowed both civilian-transition and regime-cabinet rewards with no major exclusive commitment. Replace this with the three visible institutional paths.

The previous End the Party Ban focus removed Rule by Decree. Party legality is insufficient: require genuine end of the relevant emergency/decree authority, or move removal to the constitutional milestone.
Allow an actual interim civilian cabinet before the election; reserve party-specific long-term government programmes for actual governing authority.
Keep Papadopoulos presidential reserve powers and Markezinis cabinet distinct; do not label the historical project fully democratic.
Preserve civil claims and serious-abuse screening on both alternatives. Do not sell blanket immunity as a clean constitutional legitimacy reward.
Every suggested efficiency, legitimacy or transition effect is game design, not an empirically measured historical percentage. Numerical MD rewards need independent code/balance validation.

frus_1971.title: National Intelligence Estimate, 7 June 1971
frus_1971.provenance: Contemporary US intelligence estimate; useful for the incumbent regime and opposition, not neutral authority on legitimacy.

frus_july_1973.title: NIE 29.1-73, 19 July 1973
frus_july_1973.provenance: Contemporary assessment before the plebiscite; sections I-III describe reserve powers and factional politics. Predictions must remain predictions.

frus_markezinis.title: Embassy Athens telegram 8046, 18 November 1973
frus_markezinis.provenance: Contemporary conversation with Prime Minister Markezinis after martial law; his justification is an attributed claim, not proof of a subversive conspiracy.

frus_ioannidis.title: Embassy Athens telegram 8297, 26 November 1973
frus_ioannidis.provenance: Contemporary analysis distinguishes Ioannidis, Gizikis and Androutsopoulos. Predictions of polarisation are assessments, not scripted outcomes; footnote 2 dates the coup.

parliament.title: Hellenic Parliament: Constitutional History
parliament.provenance: Official institutional retrospective; relevant sections are junta constitutions and the 1974-1975 transition.

ert_trials.title: ERT archive 0000011094, Polytechnic trial opening, 16 October 1975
ert_trials.provenance: Contemporary audiovisual archive with dated catalogue description; documents actual court proceedings, not all final verdicts.

coe.title: Council of Europe Commissioner: The Greek case, 18 April 2007
coe.provenance: Official institutional retrospective by Thomas Hammarberg describing repression, the interstate human-rights case and later trials.

coe_greek_case.title: European Commission of Human Rights: The Greek Case
coe_greek_case.provenance: Official primary human-rights case record, previously consulted in the broader research. Do not transpose later international conventions wholesale into 1970.

final_review.scope: Focused historical and narrative review of regime paths and their generated design JSON; no engine or numerical-balance certification.
resolved_history_points: Investigations and safeguards can precede elections; completed trials are not required.
Actual civilian executive transfer, electoral mandate and constitutional ratification are separate milestones.
Limited amnesty excludes erasure of serious-abuse investigations, evidence and survivor remedies.
Actual civilian transfer ends active coercive-state packages while preserving unresolved harms.
Retained junta and supervised opening remain viable alternatives without forced collapse or external war.
qualifications: All numerical buffs, costs and durations are game-design proposals.
Continuing justice-capacity expenditure must not be described as inherent civilian inefficiency.
This pass supersedes earlier findings where they describe the older draft; source research and chronological distinctions remain applicable.
